text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.98% today, extending a partial recovery from a steeper five-day slide. The stock bounced back slightly after hitting lows of $125.27 earlier this week, with oil prices stabilizing around $96.41 per barrel domestically—up from the depths of last week's selloff but still down sharply from two weeks ago. The recovery today aligns with reports of potential talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for phased crude imports, which eased some of the supply-constraint fears that had driven prices down, though geopolitical tensions remain high with the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and Senate votes on war policy.

The two-week decline still reflects deep uncertainty around the refining margin impact of a potential diesel export ban being weighed by the Trump administration. Diesel prices have spiked to $6.51 nationally, triggering warnings from big business, but if exports are restricted, refiners would likely cut production rather than sustain high margins—ultimately offering only temporary relief at the pump. For an integrated oil and gas company like this one, the competing pressures of elevated fuel demand pushing crude prices higher against the threat of production cuts on the refining side are keeping the stock volatile.
